contexts.text: (Aristotle) called the soul or spirit of man pneuma, (which he believed to be) an unseen vitality, like something of ether... SE 3954.
They have no other idea of it than as of a pneuma, or a wind...
It is believed that the Angels subsist above the atmosphere as pneumata...
Idea as of wind, air, or pneuma without a form... (Compare LJCont 3, 4.)
They are not... ethereal pneumata, but men.
He had thought... that minds are as it were ethereal pneumata...
Man after death is not a pneuma, of which there is no other idea than as of a breath of wind...
If man after death were such a pneuma, and thus a breath of wind...
Like a bird put into a pneumatic siphon...
Idea that... Spirits and Angels are pneumata, concerning which the idea is as of ether, air, breath, or wind.
It is believed that human souls after death are pneumata... TCR 792.
(Wolff said) that the soul is nothing but a pneuma...
Many of the learned... have had the idea about the soul as of a pneuma...
Otherwise those who call the soul respiration, thought, pneuma.
They say that men after death are pneumata without eyes, ears, etc.
